title: A cache-write total and its breakdown disagreeing both ways, with a price and without
matrix: input, output, cache-read and cache-write breakdowns
policy: P9 (decided on #58): flat > breakdown keeps the flat total, tier unresolved, costed at least at the cheaper tier's rate (a minimum, apart from known costs). Breakdown > flat (an explicit flat 0 included) counts the larger provisionally: the flat total tier-unresolved, the rest disputed, unpriced, and reported as a quantity conflict. An invalid tier never matches. Without a price everything is unknown, minimum included. Conflicts survive streamed growth.
derivation: Haiku 4.5, each [1, 1] before growth: a flat 300 vs 100+100 -> 300 unresolved. b flat 100 vs 200+100 -> 100 unresolved, 200 disputed. c flat 0 vs 50+30 -> 80 disputed. d no flat -> 5m 40, 1h 60. e 30 = 10+20 -> 5m 10, 1h 20. f 5m "x" -> 20 unresolved, flawed. Haiku [6, 6, 50, 80, 0, 6], unresolved 420, disputed 280 = 842. claude-test-1 h flat 10 vs 30 -> [1, 1], 10 unresolved, 20 disputed = 32, all unpriced. m1 (msg_42m only) and m2 (req_42m only), claude-test-1, each flat 5 vs 5+5 -> [1, 1], 5 unresolved, 5 disputed: 12 each, incomplete. Step 1: 874 + 24 = 898. Known (Haiku per million: input $1, output $5, 5m $1.25, 1h $2): 6 + 30 + 62.5 + 160 = 258.5 micro-dollars; minimum 420 x $1.25 = 525 micro-dollars; 280 disputed and 32 unpriced tokens unknown. Step 2 re-logs b with output 3: growth +2 output only, its conflict unchanged: Haiku output 8, known 268.5 micro-dollars. It also writes the pair msg_42m + req_42m (#55): it takes over m1 and merges m2, which is taken back with its conflict (one group, still incomplete). claude-test-1 [2, 2, 2 calls], 15 unresolved, 25 disputed = 44. 876 + 12 = 888. Disputed in the 30 days: step 1 280 + 20 + 10 = 310, step 2 305. Before this decision, a b c and h went to 5m (300, 100, 0, 10 tokens) and the breakdowns' excess was dropped.
